message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to pay the $50 jail fine or roll for doubles.

I have $389 and two unmortgaged properties. p2 is dominant with $1511 cash and full houses on major streets. p1 is weak with only $147 and almost everything mortgaged.

p2 also holds all railroads and a get-out-of-jail card, making them extremely dangerous. p4 is bankrupt. I have already spent one turn in jail without rolling doubles; I can stay for up to three turns total.

I have two more free rolls before the fine is mandatory.

Rolling doubles gives a 1/6 chance of immediate release. Paying the $50 fine is too risky. With only $389, landing on p2's dark blue properties would bankrupt me instantly.

Baltic and Virginia generate only $4 and $12 in rent, so staying in jail avoids both rent collection and payment. Paying the fine would leave me with just $339, which is even more dangerous. Rolling doubles gives a 1/6 chance of immediate release.

Rolling doubles from jail would land me on Electric Company, Virginia Avenue, or Free Parking. Virginia is my own property, but the other spaces are owned by p1 or p2 and mostly mortgaged. I also noted that if p2 owns both utilities, landing there would cost 4x or 10x the dice roll.

Rolling doubles from jail would land me on relatively safe spaces. The only utility I could hit is Electric Company, but p1 mortgaged Water Works, so p2 only owns one utility and the rent would be negligible. Virginia is my own property, while St. James, Tennessee, and Illinois are all mortgaged by p1. Free Parking is harmless.

The dangerous properties sit far around the board. Light blues like Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut are before jail, and dark blues like Park Place and Boardwalk are after it. Rolling doubles would keep me away from those high-rent squares.

Rolling doubles from jail lands me on spaces 12 through 22, which are all safe. The nearest dangerous properties are too far away to reach with a double roll. However, once I exit the jail, I will eventually circle back around toward the light blues and dark blues and die.

Paying the $50 fine would also land me on spaces 12 through 22, which are mostly safe. However, I would lose $50 immediately and then face normal rent collection. St. Charles Place and States Avenue are owned by p2 and charge $10 each. Electric Company is another p2-owned space with low rent.

I mapped the remaining spaces 15 through 22. Pennsylvania Railroad is owned by p2 and would cost $200 if they hold all four railroads. New York Avenue is also p2's with $16 rent. St. James, Tennessee, and Kentucky are mortgaged by p1 and generate no rent. I am now checking whether space 22 is a chance or community chest.

I mapped the full Monopoly board. Space 22 is a Chance card, not a community chest.

A normal roll after paying the fine would land me on spaces 12 through 22. The worst outcome is Pennsylvania Railroad, which would cost $200 and leave me with only $139. A Chance card could also send me to Boardwalk or other dangerous squares.

Rolling doubles from jail lands on only even spaces: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, and 22. Five of those six outcomes are safe. The sixth is a dangerous Chance card at space 22. Paying the fine guarantees a random roll with no protection. The clear choice is to roll for doubles.
